column2: # Approach 1: TF-IDF Lexical Distinctiveness
# 1. Build a quanteda corpus from cleaned texts
corp <- corpus(corpus_df, docid_field = "doc_id", text_field = "text_clean")
# 2. Tokenize: lowercase, remove punctuation, numbers, symbols, and standard English stopwords
toks <- tokens(corp,
remove_punct = TRUE,
remove_numbers = TRUE,
remove_symbols = TRUE) %>%
tokens_tolower() %>%
tokens_remove(stopwords("en"))
# 3. Construct Document-Feature Matrix (DFM) and compute TF-IDF weights
dfm_counts <- dfm(toks)
dfm_tfidf_mat <- dfm_tfidf(dfm_counts)
# 4. Extract top 10 distinctive terms for each document
top_terms_list <- list()
for (doc in docnames(dfm_tfidf_mat)) {
# Sort features by TF-IDF weight descending
sorted_weights <- sort(as.matrix(dfm_tfidf_mat[doc, ])[1, ], decreasing = TRUE)
top10 <- head(sorted_weights, 10)
top_terms_list[[doc]] <- tibble(
doc_id = doc,
rank = 1:10,
term = names(top10),
tfidf = round(as.numeric(top10), 3)
# Combine into a single tidy dataframe
top_tfidf_df <- bind_rows(top_terms_list)
# Reshape into a wide comparison table (Documents as rows, Top terms 1-10 as columns)
top_terms_wide <- top_tfidf_df %>%
select(doc_id, rank, term) %>%
pivot_wider(names_from = rank, names_prefix = "top_", values_from = term)
# Display the top distinctive terms table
print(top_terms_wide, n = 23)
